content:
maria: Quick follow-up to the fused-attn RFC — proposing a sentinel-flag approach for fused QKV + bias/rope + dropout-free inference paths. Wanted to get thoughts on runtime selector semantics and safe fallback behavior.

kevin: +1 to a single-request sentinel. question: do we make it per-tenant sticky or per-request explicit?

maria: Prefer per-request explicit, with an optional tenant-level prefer_* hint. sticky falls into surprises for rollback.

anil: If we do per-request, the kernel selector needs to be cheap. We should avoid doing expensive capability probing on hot paths. Suggest a small capability bitmap cached per worker.

sara: Agree. Also need a clear compatibility matrix: model format variants that can use fused_qkv vs packed_qkv vs unfused. Ops like bias-add + rope are order sensitive.

maria: Drafted a minimal config for selector heuristics:
```json
{
  "kernel_preference": ["fused_qkv_bias_rope", "packed_qkv", "unfused"],
  "dropout_mode": "inference",
  "sentinel_flags": ["QKV_MERGED","ROPE_FUSED","NO_DROPOUT"],
  "capability_cache_ttl_s": 30
}
```

oliver: Two tradeoffs: 1) fused path reduces mem copies but makes KV cache layout nonstandard (harder for offload), 2) fused bias/rope is great for perf but fragile for custom rotary implementations.

kevin: For the KV cache issue, can runtime expose an adapter that presents canonical KV layout while underlying kernels use optimized private layout? Adapter cost must be measured.

anil: Yes — adapter layer + zero-copy view where possible. Fallback needs to guarantee numerically identical outputs (within fp tolerance). That means reference-mode unit tests and deterministic replay for eval prompts.

sara: We hit a determinism bug last week in CI when switching to dropoutless inference; RNG seeds for post-attn layernorm had subtle differences. CI note: ci-bot: test-attn-determinism flaky on pr/5243 (seed drift on cuda11.8).

ci-bot: FYI — opened: https://ci.redwood/v/5243 (test-attn-determinism) — failing 2/10 runs.

maria: Good catch. We should require a determinism test harness for any fusion rollout. Anything that changes op ordering needs a golden-suite against known prompt sets.

oliver: Also propose a graceful degradation path: if fused kernel reports "soft-unsupported" for a given sequence length or head-dim, runtime should try packed_qkv, else unfused. Avoid falling back to CPU unless explicitly allowed.

kevin: Can we encode soft-unsupported reasons to logs? E.g., "fused_qkv:unsupported=head_dim(96)" so SRE can see why traffic hit fallback.

maria: Yes, logs + per-route metrics. Plan: emit a per-request tag (kernel_selected, fallback_reason) in trace spans. That feeds the Console and can trigger regression alerts.

anil: One more: rollout strategy. Start with small canary percent on dedicated pools, monitor perf + correctness, then widen. For critical tenants, allow a forced "no-fusion" flag server-side until validated.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: canary=5% on dedicated-gpu-pool-3 at 2026-06-12T02:00Z. Auto-rollback on correctness alert.

sara: For interface, prefer a compact request-level header: `X-Attention-Mode: fused_qkv_bias_rope;prefer=true` rather than large JSON in payload. Simpler for proxies.

maria: Good idea. We'll add both: header hint for low-overhead routing and request body sentinel for fine-grained opt-ins.

oliver: Tests to add: microbench (latency/p99), golden-regression (token-by-token diffs), KV-cache offload integration, and memory-safety fuzzing for rope indexing.

kevin: I'll sketch the short RFC follow-up with the sentinel semantics, capability bitmap, logging fields, and rollout checklist. Will ping infra for capability cache implementation.

maria: Thanks — let's keep this thread as the central follow-up. Ping me when draft is up. :thumbsup:
